BRIEF_COLS.label: Who Meridian Is
BRIEF_COLS.text: Integrated health system and health plan operating Epic as core EHR, with a fragmented on-prem analytics estate (SQL Server, Tableau, Power BI, SAS) and an outsourced analytics managed services provider consuming ~80% of delivery capacity on maintenance.

BRIEF_COLS.label: Where They Want to Go
BRIEF_COLS.text: Seven enterprise use cases are in scope: unified clinical + claims lakehouse, governed AI/LLM foundation, call center optimization, provider quality, cost transparency, payment integrity, and automated close. AWS and Databricks are the target platform direction — not yet production-ready.

BRIEF_COLS.label: What Is Blocking Progress
BRIEF_COLS.text: No certified medallion architecture, no patient/member identity spine, no formal data governance, no certified semantic layer, and no AI audit trail evidence. Provider contract terms are not digitized in governed form. All seven use cases require evidence closure before value can be quantified.

BRIEF_COLS.label: What Nexus Can Do Now
BRIEF_COLS.text: Nexus has mapped the enterprise context across 19 dimensions and 146 evidence references. It can surface use case hypotheses, identify gap-to-decision chains, and prioritize evidence collection. It cannot yet produce decision-grade sourcing outputs or quantified value claims.

PRIORITIES.title: Close the lakehouse foundation evidence gap
PRIORITIES.detail: Epic Clarity, Claims, and Pharmacy data harmonization must be certified before the unified clinical + claims lakehouse use case can advance. AWS/Databricks medallion architecture is aspirational — not yet evidenced.

PRIORITIES.title: Establish formal data governance and semantic layer
PRIORITIES.detail: No certified semantic layer and no formal governance operating model exist. This blocks all seven use cases, particularly AI/LLM automation, where audit trail and data quality rule evidence are also absent.

PRIORITIES.title: Digitize provider contract terms and certify attribution
PRIORITIES.detail: Provider contract terms are not in governed digital form. Attribution ownership is unproven. Both gaps block cost transparency and provider quality use cases from reaching decision grade.

PRIORITIES.title: Govern contact center transcripts and certify intent taxonomy
PRIORITIES.detail: Transcript governance, real-time CRM integration, and member identity linkage are all unproven. Call center optimization cannot advance to agent-assist or next-best-action without these foundations.

PRIORITIES.title: Certify payment integrity model lineage and recovery workflows
PRIORITIES.detail: SAS-based payment integrity models lack governed lineage. Provider entity resolution is unproven. Investigation and recovery tracking workflows are not yet evidenced, preventing leakage quantification.

SIGNALS.quote: Unified clinical + claims lakehouse is promising, but strategy is not decision-grade until Epic Clarity evidence closes — no certified medallion architecture.
Governed data foundation for AI/LLM automation is promising, but not decision-grade until Epic Clarity evidence closes — no formal data governance.
Call center optimization is promising, but not decision-grade until contact center transcript evidence closes — transcript governance not yet evidenced.
End-to-end cost transparency is promising, but not decision-grade until Claims administration platform evidence closes — provider contract terms not digitized in governed form.

DEC_CAN: Identify which of the 7 use cases has the shortest evidence-closure path
Map which systems must provide certified evidence before each use case can advance
Prioritize governance investments (semantic layer, data quality rules, audit trail) that unblock multiple use cases simultaneously
Assess managed services contract risk given ~80% maintenance load limiting net-new delivery
Sequence the AWS/Databricks platform build against use case readiness requirements
Identify which executive stakeholders own each evidence gap and assign closure accountability
DEC_CANNOT: Quantify realized savings or ROI for any use case — baselines and owner sign-off are not yet in place
Confirm AWS or Databricks as production-ready — no certified medallion architecture is evidenced
Assert that HEDIS/STAR outputs are audited or that provider attribution is accepted
Claim LLM or AI workflows are production-ready — no governance, semantic layer, or audit trail exists
Confirm provider contract economics — terms are not digitized in governed form
Assert that real-time agent assist or member-experience lift is live in the contact center

GAPS.title: No certified medallion architecture (AWS/Databricks)

GAPS.title: No formal data governance operating model

GAPS.title: No certified semantic layer
GAPS.blocks: AI/LLM, cost transparency, and automated close use cases cannot produce governed outputs. SQL Server mart sprawl creates duplicated, ungoverned business rules.

GAPS.title: No patient/member identity spine loaded
GAPS.blocks: Unified lakehouse and call center optimization both require a resolved member identity. Claims, pharmacy, and EMR data cannot be joined without it.

GAPS.title: Provider contract terms not digitized in governed form
GAPS.blocks: End-to-end cost transparency and provider quality use cases cannot produce margin or attribution outputs. Capitation and value-based contract logic remain in manual documents.

GAPS.title: Transcript governance and intent taxonomy not certified
GAPS.blocks: Call center optimization cannot advance to agent assist or next-best-action. Real-time CRM integration and member identity linkage are also unproven.

GAPS.title: Rules and model lineage not governed; provider entity resolution unproven
GAPS.blocks: Payment integrity and leakage reduction cannot quantify recoveries. SAS model lineage is ungoverned. Investigation and recovery tracking workflows are not evidenced.

GAPS.title: Close workflow integration unproven; finance semantic layer not evidenced
GAPS.blocks: Automated close and reporting use case cannot advance. Manual reporting maintenance load and ungoverned metric definitions prevent close-cycle acceleration.

USE_CASES.name: Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse
USE_CASES.fn: Enterprise Data and Analytics / Clinical Operations / Health Plan Operations
USE_CASES.value: Governed longitudinal patient/member view enabling population health, cost, and quality analytics. Value quantifiable only after EMR, claims, pharmacy, identity, medallion, and governance evidence are certified.
USE_CASES.gate: Epic Clarity medallion architecture + patient identity spine + claims/pharmacy harmonization + AWS/Databricks foundation
USE_CASES.why_this_is_top_5: CEO, CMO, and CDAO all cite this as the foundational strategic priority. It is the prerequisite platform for four of the other six use cases.

USE_CASES.name: Governed Data Foundation for AI / LLM Automation
USE_CASES.fn: Enterprise Data and Analytics / Health Plan Operations / Finance and Actuarial
USE_CASES.value: Enables prior-auth, coding, and utilization management automation. Value quantifiable only after governance, semantic ownership, lineage, and control evidence are in place and workflow baselines are captured.
USE_CASES.gate: Formal data governance operating model + certified semantic layer + AI audit trail + data quality rules
USE_CASES.why_this_is_top_5: CEO, CFO, CIO, CDAO, Health Plan Ops, and Procurement all flag this as a top priority. It is the governance prerequisite for all AI/LLM use cases.

USE_CASES.name: Payment Integrity and Leakage Reduction
USE_CASES.fn: Health Plan Operations / Finance and Actuarial / Analytics
USE_CASES.value: Reduces claims leakage through anomaly detection, FWA identification, and billing pattern analysis. Value quantifiable only after claims anomaly features, provider resolution, rules lineage, and recovery workflow evidence are governed.
USE_CASES.gate: SAS model lineage governance + provider entity resolution + investigation workflow evidence + recovery tracking
USE_CASES.why_this_is_top_5: CFO and Chief Experience Officer both flag payment integrity as a top strategic priority. SAS estate is the current detection platform but lacks governed lineage.

USE_CASES.name: End-to-End Cost Transparency
USE_CASES.fn: Finance and Actuarial / Health Plan Operations / Network Contracting
USE_CASES.value: Creates cost-of-care and margin visibility across claims, capitation, and provider contracts. Value quantifiable only after claims, capitation, contract, and GL reconciliation evidence is governed and finance/actuarial baseline is signed off.
USE_CASES.gate: Provider contract digitization + claims/GL calendar alignment + cost allocation rules + margin semantic model
USE_CASES.why_this_is_top_5: CEO, CFO, and CDAO all cite cost transparency as a top priority. Provider contract terms not being in governed digital form is the single largest blocker.

USE_CASES.name: Call Center Optimization
USE_CASES.fn: Contact Center and Member Experience / Health Plan Operations
USE_CASES.value: Improves agent assist and next-best-action using transcripts, CRM cases, and claims status. Value quantifiable only after transcript, CRM, claims, intent, and QA-label evidence is governed and baseline AHT/containment/FCR data are loaded.
USE_CASES.gate: Transcript governance + real-time CRM integration + intent taxonomy certification + member identity linkage
USE_CASES.why_this_is_top_5: CEO, CFO, and CIO all flag call center optimization. Chief Experience Officer owns member experience outcomes. Contact center platform and CRM are current-core but ungoverned for analytics.

rows.business_name: CFO / Finance & Value interview evidence
rows.context_item: CFO / Finance & Value says AI Benefits Realization Ledger needs FP&A validation and usage extracts required: The CFO would not let Tower count AI spend as delivered value until the usage extract, operational KPI movement, and FP&A validation all reconcile to the same program code. Copilot, ServiceNow, Workday, and developer productivity pilots can be measured, but Member Service AI Assist remains a candidate with no approved funding.

rows.business_name: Chief Experience Officer / Member Experience interview evidence
rows.context_item: Chief Experience Officer / Member Experience says Member Service Agent Assist Transformation needs Approved business case, baseline, and PHI controls required: No. Member Service AI Assist is a candidate/discovery opportunity. The funded work is the contact-center platform, knowledge foundation, data readiness, and AI governance controls. A separate Moves business case is required before AI Assist receives approved funding.

rows.business_name: CISO / Security interview evidence
rows.context_item: CISO / Security says AI Governance / Model Risk Controls needs HITL, audit logging, and model-risk evidence required: PHI access logging, human-in-the-loop validation, prompt/audit trails, and model inventory ownership must be complete before service, Workday, or member-facing AI pilots scale beyond controlled pilots.

rows.business_name: Contact Center / Member Service Operations interview evidence
rows.context_item: Contact Center / Member Service Operations says Contact Center Platform / Knowledge Modernization needs AHT, FCR, transfer, CSAT, and QA baselines required: Operations needs call reason, AHT, FCR, transfer, knowledge-search, QA, and escalation baselines before AI Assist is funded. Usage data from Genesys and the knowledge platform should prove the foundation first.

rows.business_name: CIO / Enterprise Technology interview evidence
rows.context_item: CIO / Enterprise Technology says FY26 AI spend governance needs Budget, program, and benefits ledger ties required: The CIO should show AI spend as tagged inside approved platforms and programs: Copilot, ServiceNow, Workday, GitHub Copilot, Databricks, cloud AI services, and governance controls. It should not be described as a separate AI budget or as a delivered financial outcome.

findings: Profile confidence is split 50/50: the organizational identity is high-confidence, but the operating-model sizing assumptions driving all use-case business cases are low-confidence and finance-unattested — creating a planning risk that cascades across all seven use cases.
No owners, systems, or use-case linkages are registered against the profile dimension, meaning accountability for evidence closure is unassigned and no escalation path exists.

AWS and Databricks are recorded as target-state direction only; no certified platform foundation evidence is loaded, so profile-level scale assumptions cannot be validated against an actual infrastructure baseline.

Until Finance attests the operating-model sizing assumptions, no use-case ROI projection — lakehouse, AI/LLM, payment integrity, cost transparency, or call center — can be presented as decision-grade to the CFO or Board.

findings: Epic Clarity and Caboodle are current-core clinical reporting assets, but no certified medallion architecture connects them to claims or pharmacy — the lakehouse use case cannot advance without this evidence gate closed.

Four parallel BI tools (Tableau, Power BI, SAS, SQL Server marts) produce duplicated, ungoverned metric definitions; this fragmentation directly blocks the governed semantic layer required for AI/LLM automation and cost transparency.

narrative_sections.context_confidence_summary: Nexus has loaded 19 source-backed dimensions covering 3,987 source rows and 147 evidence references. Confidence is high on enterprise profile, system inventory, and executive use case intent. Confidence is directional on platform readiness and value hypotheses. AWS and Databricks are aspirational targets, not confirmed production foundations. All seven use cases require evidence closure before any dimension reaches decision grade.
narrative_sections.evidence_gaps_summary: Four high-severity gaps block every use case simultaneously: no certified medallion architecture, no formal data governance operating model, no certified semantic layer, and no patient/member identity spine. Three additional high-severity gaps are use-case-specific: provider contract terms are not digitized in governed form, transcript governance and intent taxonomy are uncertified, and SAS payment integrity model lineage is ungoverned. No realized value can be claimed until baselines and owner sign-off are in place.
narrative_sections.use_cases_summary: Seven enterprise use cases are identified and source-backed: unified clinical and claims lakehouse, governed AI/LLM foundation, call center optimization, provider quality and performance, end-to-end cost transparency, payment integrity and leakage reduction, and automated close and reporting. All are in planning stage. The lakehouse and AI/LLM governance use cases are foundational prerequisites for the remaining five. No use case has cleared its evidence gate.
narrative_sections.use_cases_portfolio_view: All seven use cases are in planning stage. Lakehouse and AI/LLM governance are foundational prerequisites; close their evidence gates first. Cost transparency and payment integrity can advance in parallel once governance is established. Call center optimization and provider quality follow. Automated close depends on a certified finance semantic layer and is the final sequencing step.
narrative_sections.proof_summary: Nexus has assembled 147 evidence references spanning executive interviews, system records, risk and gap documentation, industry patterns, and data asset mappings. The evidence base confirms system inventory, use case intent, and a 24-item risk and gap register across all seven use cases. No evidence confirms production AI readiness, realized savings, a certified medallion architecture, or a formal data governance operating model. All value hypotheses remain planning-grade.

narrative_sections.enterprise_brief_title: Meridian Health System: Seven Use Cases, Zero Decision-Grade Evidence Closures
narrative_sections.enterprise_brief_summary: Meridian Health System operates as an integrated health system and health plan anchored on Epic Hyperspace, Clarity, and Caboodle, with a fragmented on-premise analytics estate spanning SQL Server, Tableau, Power BI, and SAS. An outsourced analytics managed services provider consumes an estimated 80% of delivery capacity on maintenance, leaving minimal bandwidth for net-new strategic work. AWS and Databricks represent the target platform direction — neither is production-ready, and no certified medallion architecture has been evidenced. Ten-plus executive stakeholder groups — CEO, CFO, CIO, CDAO, CMO, Chief Experience Officer, Health Plan Operations, Privacy, Procurement, and the Program Office — have each confirmed seven enterprise use cases as strategic priorities: unified clinical and claims lakehouse, governed AI/LLM foundation, call center optimization, provider quality and performance, end-to-end cost transparency, payment integrity and leakage reduction, and automated close and reporting. Every use case is in planning stage. None has reached decision grade. The four pervasive blockers — no certified medallion architecture, no formal data governance operating model, no certified semantic layer, and no patient/member identity spine — must be resolved before Nexus can produce sourcing-event outputs or quantified value claims. The executive decision now is: which evidence closure to fund first, and who owns accountability for each gap.

quality_assessment.story_strength: The enterprise story is coherent and well-bounded: Meridian is an integrated payer-provider with a strong Epic clinical core, a fragmented on-prem analytics estate, and seven high-priority use cases that are all blocked by the same four foundational gaps (medallion architecture, data governance, semantic layer, identity spine). The narrative is honest about what Nexus can and cannot support, and the evidence gap structure gives executives a clear action agenda. The story would reach full McKinsey bar if baseline metrics (AHT, close cycle days, leakage rate) were loaded and value hypotheses could be bounded with directional ranges.
known_weaknesses: No baseline metrics loaded for any use case — AHT, close cycle, leakage rate, and HEDIS/STAR scores are all absent, preventing even directional value ranging.
Commercial contract terms are not evidenced for any vendor — total IT spend, vendor concentration risk, and renewal exposure cannot be assessed.
AWS and Databricks platform readiness is aspirational only — no network, security, IAM, or medallion architecture evidence exists, making the lakehouse timeline unassessable.
Finance and Actuarial function is candidate-status only — cost transparency and automated close use cases lack a confirmed finance owner.
Provider contract terms are in manual documents — digitization scope and timeline are unknown, blocking two use cases from advancing.
Workforce roles dimension has zero active rows — all 216 rows are candidate, meaning role-level accountability for evidence closure cannot be assigned.
quality_assessment.why_this_is_better_than_current: The current state at Meridian is a fragmented analytics estate with duplicated business rules, an outsourced managed services provider consuming ~80% of capacity on maintenance, and no shared governance model. Nexus provides the first integrated view of all 19 enterprise dimensions, maps the 24 specific evidence gaps blocking the 7 use cases, and gives the executive team a structured evidence closure agenda — replacing ad hoc stakeholder interviews with a governed, traceable context layer.
